domain_label: User and Cognition Modeling (adaptive UX, non-clinical)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is adaptive UX personalization via cognitive signal modeling; clinical/medical use is out of scope
user state is modeled as probabilistic time-varying signal, not a fixed label or diagnosis
dual-process framing is used as an engineering convenience model, not a clinical claim
exclusions: clinical cognitive assessment, neuropsychological testing, or psychiatric diagnosis
treatment of cognitive disorders or mental health conditions
use of protected health information (PHI) or medical records
criminal justice or employment decisions based on cognitive modeling

competency_questions.question: What cognitive architecture framing grounds adaptive UX routing decisions?
How is the dual-process model used to route between simple and complex UX without clinical claims?
How is user expertise level estimated probabilistically from behavioral signals?
How does the system handle cold-start for new users with no history?
How is educational background estimated and used for difficulty calibration?
How are fatigue and time-of-day effects modeled as UX signals?
How is cognitive overload detected in real time and how does the UX respond?
Which cognitive biases are catalogued and how are their UX fingerprints defined?
How are bias mitigation interventions designed to avoid crossing into coercion or dark patterns?
How is ecological rationality applied to risk and uncertainty communication in the UX?
How are user intents classified and used to gate difficulty and content personalization?
How are stale user-state beliefs managed and how is drift in signals detected?
How are ethical bounds and privacy constraints enforced in the cognitive modeling pipeline?
How is adaptive personalization evaluated and what guardrail metrics prevent exploitation?

glossary.definition: Kahneman System 1 (fast, automatic, heuristic) and System 2 (slow, deliberate, analytic) cognitive modes used as an engineering routing heuristic in adaptive UX
Bayesian probability distribution over novice/intermediate/expert tiers updated from behavioral interaction signals
The working-memory demand imposed by an interface task; managed via difficulty control and scaffolding to stay within user capacity
Probabilistic proxy for elevated cognitive fatigue derived from session behavioral patterns; a UX personalization input, not a health measurement
Systematic deviation from rational inference caused by heuristic shortcuts; catalogued with UX signal fingerprints for targeted mitigation in adaptive interfaces
Temporary support structures (hints, examples, progressive disclosure) calibrated to user expertise that are faded as mastery accumulates
Gigerenzer framework holding that heuristics are rational when matched to the information structure of the user environment; drives natural-frequency and icon-array UX formatting
The state where no user behavioral history exists, requiring population priors and onboarding signals to initialize the user-state posterior
A self-reinforcing feedback loop where adaptive difficulty locks to a narrow range, reducing exposure to appropriate challenge; requires diversity injection to prevent

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for cognitive user modeling and adaptive UX work units in absence of supplied datasets
Kahneman D. Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011). Dual-process theory, cognitive biases, heuristics.
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Kahneman, D. (2011). Thinking, Fast and Slow. Farrar, Straus and Giroux.
grounding_limits: theoretical; empirical replication record mixed on specific biases

source_registry.description: Gigerenzer G. Rationality for Mortals (2008). Ecological rationality, natural frequencies.
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Gigerenzer, G. (2008). Rationality for Mortals. Oxford University Press.
grounding_limits: primarily focused on statistical reasoning; UX application is extension by analogy

source_registry.description: Sternberg R.J. and Sternberg K. Cognitive Psychology 6th ed (2012). Working memory, attention, metacognition.
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Sternberg, R.J. & Sternberg, K. (2012). Cognitive Psychology, 6th edition. Wadsworth.
grounding_limits: textbook-level; empirical claims vary across research strands

nodes.definition: Establish the dual-process (System 1/System 2) and working-memory-capacity framing that underpins all adaptive UX decisions; defines when fast heuristic vs slow deliberate routing applies.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: major revision to dual-process empirical literature

pros.claim: Provides principled basis for when to simplify vs enrich UX
pros.example: System-1 users get defaults; System-2 users get advanced controls

cons.claim: Dual-process framing is debated; folk-psychology risk if applied naively
cons.example: Mistaking speed for System 1 mislabels deliberate fast experts

failure_modes: conflating speed with System-1 activation
ignoring domain expertise modulating system usage
acceptance_tests: framing doc reviewed by UX researcher
routing rules cover all user-state combinations
revisit_triggers: Kahneman dual-process framing substantially revised in literature

nodes.definition: Infer user expertise level as a probability distribution over novice/intermediate/expert using observable behavioral signals (response latency, error rate, help-seeking frequency, vocabulary usage) as a UX personalization signal, not a credential.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: interaction modality or user population shifts

pros.claim: Continuous posterior enables graceful difficulty ramp without discrete jumps
pros.example: Expert posterior rises as user solves advanced queries without help

cons.claim: Cold-start problem: first session has uninformative prior leading to conservative defaults
cons.example: New user gets novice defaults even if expert

failure_modes: conflating domain expertise with general cognitive ability
anchoring on first session behavior
acceptance_tests: posterior CI width <0.3 before tier promotion
expertise estimate updates monotone with accumulating evidence in simulation
revisit_triggers: new interaction modality added requiring feature recalibration
major user population shift detected

nodes.definition: Estimate user domain-relevant educational background and prior knowledge depth from vocabulary complexity, question framing, and reference patterns as a probabilistic UX signal for content difficulty calibration.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: user language distribution or domain vocabulary shifts

pros.claim: Vocabulary-based estimation is low-overhead and scalable without user surveys
pros.example: Readability model detects background from first 3 queries

cons.claim: Vocabulary proxy confounded by query ambiguity or second-language use
cons.example: Non-native speakers appear lower-knowledge than they are

failure_modes: confounding second-language use with low domain knowledge
overfitting vocabulary model to narrow corpus
acceptance_tests: cross-linguistic fairness test passes
background estimate decorrelates from native-language proxy after calibration
revisit_triggers: multilingual user base grows requiring language-agnostic proxies
domain vocabulary shifts with new product releases

nodes.definition: Model user cognitive fatigue and time-of-day load effects as a probabilistic time-varying signal using session duration, error-rate trajectory, response-time drift, and circadian proxy (local time) to adaptively reduce UX complexity when fatigue is elevated.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: device context shift or session-pattern change

pros.claim: Prevents UX complexity spikes during high-fatigue windows reducing error rates
pros.example: Late-night high-error sessions auto-simplify to confirmation flows

cons.claim: Fatigue proxy from error rate confounded by novel task difficulty
cons.example: New complex task looks like fatigue; system incorrectly simplifies

failure_modes: confounding novel task difficulty with fatigue signal
ignoring timezone errors in local-time proxy
acceptance_tests: fatigue signal decorrelates from task-novelty indicator in holdout
circadian proxy validated against self-reported fatigue in UX study
revisit_triggers: session length norms shift (mobile vs desktop contexts)
timezone detection accuracy degrades

nodes.definition: Maintain an enumerated catalog of cognitive biases relevant to UX (anchoring, availability heuristic, framing effect, sunk-cost, confirmation bias, overconfidence) with mitigation strategies and UX signal fingerprints that indicate when each bias is active.
outputs: bias catalog with UX signal fingerprints

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new bias research invalidates or adds catalog entries

pros.claim: Enables proactive mitigation by detecting bias-indicative interaction patterns
pros.example: Anchoring detected when user fixates on first-shown value; reframe triggered

cons.claim: Catalog can become stale as new biases are identified or old ones reframed
cons.example: Overconfidence bias definition varies across literature strands

failure_modes: over-applying bias labels to normal variation
ignoring bias interaction effects
acceptance_tests: catalog covers at least 8 named biases with distinct UX fingerprints
each bias entry has at least one testable mitigation strategy
revisit_triggers: new high-impact bias identified in UX research
existing bias mitigation strategy proves ineffective in A/B test

nodes.definition: Apply targeted UX interventions (reframing, choice architecture nudges, multiple-reference-point presentation, confirmation prompts) to reduce the influence of detected cognitive biases on user decisions without coercing choices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ethics policy changes or new dark-pattern classification published

pros.claim: Nudge-based mitigation preserves autonomy while reducing harmful bias influence
pros.example: Show multiple anchor prices to counteract single-anchor anchoring bias

cons.claim: Nudges can cross into manipulation if designed without ethical constraints
cons.example: Reframing a loss as gain can deceive rather than inform

failure_modes: crossing from debiasing into manipulation
applying mitigation without detected bias signal
acceptance_tests: ethical review checklist passed for each intervention type
user autonomy metric not degraded by mitigation in A/B
revisit_triggers: ethics policy updated (revise all interventions)
new dark-pattern classification covers an existing strategy

nodes.definition: Dynamically adjust question complexity, content depth, and scaffolding level using a PID-like feedback loop on user performance signals (accuracy, latency, help-seeking) informed by expertise and fatigue posteriors.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: user population performance distribution shifts

pros.claim: Continuous feedback loop prevents both boredom and overwhelm zones
pros.example: Novice plateau detection triggers hint injection before disengagement

cons.claim: PID control can oscillate if gain parameters poorly tuned for user variance
cons.example: Over-responsive system flip-flops difficulty causing user frustration

failure_modes: oscillating difficulty causing disorientation
ignoring fatigue when computing difficulty setpoint
acceptance_tests: difficulty oscillation amplitude <15% in simulation
scaffolding level monotone decreasing with demonstrated mastery
revisit_triggers: performance signal latency increases
new user segment with bimodal performance distribution discovered

nodes.definition: Classify user queries into intent types (informational, navigational, transactional, exploratory) using NLP signals and session context, feeding downstream difficulty routing and personalization logic.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new intent type emerges or product taxonomy changes

pros.claim: Intent class gates downstream difficulty and content type reducing irrelevant scaffolding
pros.example: Exploratory intent triggers concept-map UX; transactional triggers minimal-click flow

cons.claim: Short queries are highly ambiguous; intent classifier confidence low at cold start
cons.example: Single-word query 'bank' equally likely financial or river intent

failure_modes: low-confidence routing defaulting to wrong intent
ignoring session history for intent smoothing
acceptance_tests: intent classifier F1 >0.78 on held-out query set
intent confidence threshold calibrated so uncertainty triggers clarification prompt
revisit_triggers: new product category creates novel intent type
query language distribution shifts

nodes.definition: Fuse multiple noisy signals (expertise, fatigue, education, intent) into a coherent user-state posterior using a Bayesian update rule; handles missing signals via marginalization and produces calibrated uncertainty intervals.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new signal dimension added or calibration drift detected

pros.claim: Handles missing signals gracefully via marginalization instead of failure
pros.example: If fatigue signal missing, marginalizes over fatigue dimension

cons.claim: Computational overhead of joint posterior grows with signal dimensionality
cons.example: Joint over 5 dimensions requires approximation for real-time use

failure_modes: prior specification errors propagate into all downstream decisions
overconfident posteriors from underestimated likelihoods
acceptance_tests: posterior coverage test: 90% CI contains true state in simulation 90% of time
update latency <50ms at p99 in production load test
revisit_triggers: new signal dimension added requiring prior specification
calibration drift detected in posterior coverage test

nodes.definition: Initialize user-state posteriors for first-time users with no behavioral history using population priors, optional onboarding signals (self-reported role, goals), and context features (device type, referral source).

excluded: assuming expert defaults for all users

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new market launch or regulatory change affecting onboarding

pros.claim: Onboarding signals dramatically reduce cold-start error even with 2-3 questions
pros.example: Role self-report alone cuts novice misclassification by ~40% heuristically

cons.claim: Optional onboarding surveys have low completion rates reducing cold-start quality
cons.example: Mobile users skip onboarding at high rates reducing signal quality

failure_modes: forcing onboarding reducing new-user retention
using PII-adjacent signals without consent
acceptance_tests: cold-start posterior converges to equilibrium within N<=5 interactions in simulation
onboarding questions GDPR-reviewed and optional
revisit_triggers: GDPR interpretation changes requiring onboarding redesign
new market with different population prior distribution

nodes.definition: Define and enforce hard constraints preventing the adaptive UX system from crossing into clinical, diagnostic, or therapeutic territory; includes explicit scope declarations, refusal rules, and user-facing disclaimers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: regulatory change or ethics policy revision

pros.claim: Hard refusal rules prevent liability from clinical overreach
pros.example: System refuses to label user as cognitively impaired or recommend clinical action

cons.claim: Overly broad ethics rules can hobble legitimate personalization features
cons.example: Blanket ban on cognitive terms blocks useful expertise framing

failure_modes: scope creep into clinical territory
ethics rules so broad they eliminate core functionality
acceptance_tests: all bias mitigation interventions pass ethics review
no node definition uses diagnostic framing (automated check)
revisit_triggers: new jurisdiction with stricter AI ethics regulations
clinical-adjacent feature requested by product team

nodes.definition: Detect cognitive overload states from interaction signals (error bursts, help-seek spikes, abandonment precursors, response-time bimodality) and trigger UI simplification or scaffolding injection before task abandonment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: interaction modality change or abandonment pattern shift

pros.claim: Real-time detection enables preemptive simplification preventing costly abandonment
pros.example: Error burst within 60s triggers progressive disclosure collapse before dropout

cons.claim: Overload detector can false-positive on novel complex tasks that require difficulty
cons.example: Legitimate hard problem triggers simplification that removes necessary information

failure_modes: false-positive simplification on legitimately hard tasks
latency in detection making intervention too late
acceptance_tests: overload precision >0.80 vs abandonment ground truth in holdout
false-positive rate on hard-task cohort <0.15
revisit_triggers: new interaction modality requires overload signal recalibration
abandonment patterns shift due to product redesign

nodes.definition: Apply time-based decay to user-state beliefs to prevent stale expertise/fatigue estimates from dominating; uses exponential decay with configurable half-life per signal dimension and triggers re-estimation when staleness exceeds threshold.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: usage pattern changes or retention policy changes

pros.claim: Prevents stale expertise estimates after long inactivity from harming new-session UX
pros.example: 30-day inactive user expertise belief decays to near-prior before next session

cons.claim: Aggressive decay erases legitimate long-term expertise and frustrates returning experts
cons.example: Expert user returning after vacation gets novice treatment

failure_modes: decay too aggressive erasing long-term expertise
decay too slow locking fatigue estimate into wrong state
acceptance_tests: returning-expert test: after 2-week absence expertise tier preserved at >80% original confidence
staleness flag triggers re-estimation within 2 interactions
revisit_triggers: usage pattern changes (seasonal users)
business decision to retain longer state for premium users

nodes.definition: Segment user population into behaviorally-coherent persona clusters; use cluster membership as informative prior for Bayesian user-state initialization, reducing cold-start uncertainty.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fairness audit fails or population distribution shifts

pros.claim: Cluster priors cut cold-start error for new users whose cluster is identifiable early
pros.example: Device and referral source predicts cluster with ~70% accuracy heuristically

cons.claim: Cluster assignment can encode demographic proxies leading to fairness concerns
cons.example: Cluster based on device type may proxy for income level

failure_modes: encoding protected-attribute proxies in clusters
over-segmentation creating unstable clusters with few members
acceptance_tests: cluster fairness audit: no cluster correlates >0.3 with protected attributes
cluster stability: <10% reassignment rate week-over-week
revisit_triggers: user population distribution shifts making clusters stale
fairness audit flags proxy correlation

nodes.definition: Define the evaluation framework for adaptive UX personalization: A/B test design (holdout of adaptive feature), offline simulation on historical logs, metric selection (task completion, error rate, satisfaction), and guardrail metrics (autonomy, fairness).

included: A/B test design for adaptive feature

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: primary metric changes or fairness guardrail policy updated

pros.claim: A/B holdout provides causal estimate of adaptive personalization value
pros.example: Control arm keeps static UX; treatment arm gets adaptive difficulty

cons.claim: Adaptive features harm A/B power because between-user variance is high
cons.example: Small personalization lift is hard to detect in short A/B windows

failure_modes: A/B contamination from shared infrastructure
ignoring guardrail metrics in pursuit of primary metric lift
acceptance_tests: A/B protocol passes statistical review (power >0.80 for target effect size)
guardrail metric dashboard reviewed before ship decision
revisit_triggers: new primary metric defined requiring evaluation redesign
fairness guardrail threshold tightened by policy

nodes.definition: Detect user overconfidence patterns (high confidence with low accuracy, premature task closure, skipping verification steps) as a specific cognitive bias signal requiring targeted mitigation in the UX flow.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task type changes or user perception study indicates patronizing UX

pros.claim: Prompting verification at overconfidence detection reduces downstream error costs
pros.example: Overconfident user skipping review step gets soft confirmation gate injected

cons.claim: Verification prompts perceived as patronizing by genuinely expert users
cons.example: Expert correctly skipping obvious step gets interrupted by false-positive gate

failure_modes: false-positive verification gates frustrating experts
conflating low-effort with overconfidence
acceptance_tests: overconfidence precision >0.75 on labeled interaction set
expert false-positive rate <0.20 on expert-annotated cohort
revisit_triggers: task type changes making verification-skip a valid expert shortcut
user study reveals prompts perceived as distrust

nodes.definition: Deliver contextual scaffolding (hints, worked examples, analogies, progressive disclosure) calibrated to user expertise and fatigue posteriors; fades scaffolding as mastery signals accumulate.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new content domain or mastery signal definition changes

pros.claim: Fading scaffolding with mastery prevents learned helplessness and promotes autonomy
pros.example: Hint frequency decreases by 20% per successful unscaffolded task completion

cons.claim: Scaffolding library maintenance is costly; stale examples confuse users
cons.example: Outdated code example in scaffolding uses deprecated API

failure_modes: over-scaffolding preventing skill development
scaffolding library staleness
acceptance_tests: scaffolding fade test: fade rate correlates with mastery signal r>0.6 in simulation
scaffolding library reviewed quarterly
revisit_triggers: new content domain added requiring scaffolding library expansion
mastery signal definition changes

nodes.definition: Govern collection, retention, and use of behavioral signals for cognitive modeling; enforce data minimization, purpose limitation, user consent, and right-to-deletion for all user-state data.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new jurisdiction regulation or deletion SLA breach

pros.claim: Data minimization reduces regulatory risk while preserving modeling quality for key signals
pros.example: Retain only last-30-day interaction features; delete raw event log after aggregation

cons.claim: Aggressive deletion breaks longitudinal expertise modeling for returning users
cons.example: Right-to-deletion erases all expertise history requiring cold-start

failure_modes: retention policy too long creating GDPR liability
deletion propagation gap leaving orphan user-state records
acceptance_tests: GDPR DPIA completed and signed off
deletion workflow tested end-to-end in staging
revisit_triggers: new jurisdiction regulation
deletion SLA breach incident

nodes.definition: Continuously calibrate behavioral signals against ground-truth labels (task outcomes, satisfaction surveys, expert annotation) and detect distribution drift in signals that indicates model staleness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ground-truth labeling capacity changes or new signal added

pros.claim: Drift detection prevents silent model degradation from population shift
pros.example: PSI alert fires when feature distribution shifts >0.2, triggering investigation

cons.claim: Calibration requires labeled data which is expensive to collect continuously
cons.example: Satisfaction surveys suffer low response rate making calibration sparse

failure_modes: missing drift detection causing silent degradation
over-sensitive drift alert causing unnecessary retraining churn
acceptance_tests: calibration check automated and runs weekly
drift alert fires in <24h of injected distribution shift in staging test
revisit_triggers: ground-truth labeling capacity reduced
new signal dimension added without calibration baseline

nodes.definition: Design and deliver metacognitive prompts (self-explanation requests, prediction-before-answer, confidence polling) calibrated to user expertise and bias state to improve user self-awareness and reduce overconfidence without adding cognitive load.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new metacognition research or prompt injection point changes

pros.claim: Prediction-before-answer prompts improve calibration and learning transfer
pros.example: Ask user to predict answer before revealing it; reduces overconfidence in follow-up tasks

cons.claim: Metacognitive prompts increase cognitive load if mistimed during high-fatigue state
cons.example: Prompts during high-fatigue window cause dropout rather than reflection

failure_modes: prompting during high-fatigue state adding load
prompts perceived as distrustful by expert users
acceptance_tests: prompt delivery gated on fatigue posterior <0.6
prompt skip rate <0.40 in expert cohort
revisit_triggers: new research shows specific prompt types ineffective for target population
product redesign changes available prompt injection points

nodes.definition: Apply Gigerenzer ecological rationality framework to design risk and uncertainty communication: use natural frequencies instead of probabilities, icon arrays instead of percentages, and format information to match user cognitive environment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new risk communication formats available or numeracy model updated

pros.claim: Natural frequencies understood by broader audience than raw probabilities
pros.example: Switching to natural frequency framing improved comprehension in Gigerenzer studies

cons.claim: Numeracy-adaptive framing requires reliable numeracy estimate which is hard to collect
cons.example: Wrong numeracy estimate causes mismatch: expert shown icon array feels patronized

failure_modes: choosing wrong format for user numeracy level
conflating statistical literacy with general expertise
acceptance_tests: numeracy format selection correct for 80%+ of users in usability study
format switch A/B shows comprehension improvement
revisit_triggers: new format types available (interactive visualizations)
numeracy estimation method updated

nodes.definition: Govern the closed-loop adaptation cycle: define update frequency, prevent runaway self-reinforcing loops (filter bubble, difficulty collapse), enforce diversity injection, and set minimum exploration rates for user-state estimation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: business policy change on exploration or filter bubble detected

pros.claim: Minimum exploration rate prevents difficulty collapse to a single level for all users
pros.example: 10% random difficulty injection prevents the controller from locking to easy mode

cons.claim: Exploration injection can temporarily degrade user experience to gather information
cons.example: Random difficulty spike frustrates user who was in a productive flow state

failure_modes: filter bubble locking user into narrow difficulty band
exploration rate too high causing persistent UX degradation
acceptance_tests: filter bubble: difficulty variance within user >0.15 measured monthly
exploration rate bounded [0.05, 0.20] and configurable
revisit_triggers: business pressure to reduce exploration
new evidence shows current exploration rate causes unacceptable UX degradation

edges.why_related: dual-process framing defines what behavioral signals constitute expertise evidence
edges.benefit_of_coupling: consistent expertise estimation grounded in cognitive theory
edges.risk_of_conflict: framing change invalidates signal definitions
edges.example: COG_ARCH routing policy defines which signals count as expertise evidence

edges.why_related: cognitive load taxonomy informs what educational background signals are relevant
edges.benefit_of_coupling: principled selection of vocabulary and knowledge signals
edges.risk_of_conflict: framing change may invalidate background signal selection
edges.example: COG_ARCH cognitive load taxonomy grounds EDU_EST signal selection

edges.why_related: working memory capacity model defines fatigue operational thresholds
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fatigue thresholds grounded in cognitive capacity theory
edges.risk_of_conflict: WM model revision changes fatigue threshold calibration
edges.example: WM capacity model from COG_ARCH defines FATIGUE_EST operational bounds

edges.why_related: dual-process model determines which biases are System-1 vs System-2 phenomena
edges.benefit_of_coupling: bias catalog grounded in cognitive architecture
edges.risk_of_conflict: architecture revision may reclassify biases
edges.example: System-1 heuristics drive anchoring/availability; System-2 drives deliberate confirmation bias

edges.why_related: expertise posterior is a required input signal to the Bayesian fusion engine
edges.benefit_of_coupling: richer joint posterior from expertise dimension
edges.risk_of_conflict: EXPERT_EST failure degrades posterior quality
edges.example: expertise posterior fed to BAYES_UPDATE at each interaction

edges.why_related: education/background estimate feeds the background-knowledge dimension of the joint posterior
edges.benefit_of_coupling: background dimension adds difficulty calibration power
edges.risk_of_conflict: EDU_EST miscalibration biases joint posterior
edges.example: background estimate fused with expertise and fatigue in BAYES_UPDATE

edges.why_related: fatigue posterior feeds the time-varying fatigue dimension of the joint user-state posterior
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fatigue dimension enables load-aware personalization
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale fatigue signal corrupts joint posterior
edges.example: fatigue posterior updated every interaction and fused in BAYES_UPDATE

edges.why_related: intent class distribution conditions the joint posterior on task-type context
edges.benefit_of_coupling: intent conditioning reduces posterior uncertainty
edges.risk_of_conflict: intent miscalibration misdirects difficulty routing
edges.example: intent class gates content-type and difficulty routing within BAYES_UPDATE

edges.why_related: joint user-state posterior drives the difficulty setpoint calculation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: difficulty grounded in full probabilistic user state
edges.risk_of_conflict: posterior errors propagate to difficulty miscalibration
edges.example: ADAPT_DIFF reads expertise and fatigue dimensions from BAYES_UPDATE posterior

edges.why_related: posterior convergence speed determines when cold-start is resolved
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clear signal when cold-start phase ends
edges.risk_of_conflict: overconfident posterior may prematurely exit cold-start
edges.example: BAYES_UPDATE confidence triggers end of cold-start initialization phase

edges.why_related: temporal decay operates on the posteriors produced by BAYES_UPDATE
edges.benefit_of_coupling: decay naturally integrated into update cycle
edges.risk_of_conflict: decay mis-applied to wrong posterior dimension
edges.example: TEMPORAL_DECAY halves BAYES_UPDATE posterior confidence on configured schedule

edges.why_related: cold-start initialization provides the prior that BAYES_UPDATE updates from
edges.benefit_of_coupling: principled warm prior reduces early posterior instability
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong cold-start prior biases all early updates
edges.example: COLD_START prior injected as initial state; BAYES_UPDATE updates from it

edges.why_related: catalog fingerprints trigger specific mitigation strategies
edges.benefit_of_coupling: mitigation is precisely matched to detected bias
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale catalog fingerprints trigger wrong mitigations
edges.example: each BIAS_CATALOG entry maps to one or more BIAS_MITIG intervention types

edges.why_related: overconfidence is a catalogued bias with a specific UX fingerprint driving OVERCONF_DETECT
edges.benefit_of_coupling: overconfidence detection grounded in bias taxonomy
edges.risk_of_conflict: catalog definition change invalidates overconfidence detection logic
edges.example: OVERCONF_DETECT implements the overconfidence fingerprint from BIAS_CATALOG

edges.why_related: difficulty setpoint from ADAPT_DIFF determines scaffolding level selection
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scaffolding calibrated to current difficulty level
edges.risk_of_conflict: difficulty miscalibration causes scaffolding mismatch
edges.example: SCAFFOLDING level is a function of ADAPT_DIFF setpoint and expertise posterior

edges.why_related: overload detection provides corrective feedback to the difficulty controller
edges.benefit_of_coupling: overload signal prevents the controller from pushing into overload zone
edges.risk_of_conflict: feedback loop may oscillate if overload threshold poorly set
edges.example: OVERLOAD_DETECT fires signal back to ADAPT_DIFF to reduce difficulty setpoint

edges.why_related: ethics bounds define the acceptable intervention space for bias mitigation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: mitigation stays within safe non-coercive territory
edges.risk_of_conflict: ethics constraint violation causes regulatory risk
edges.example: BIAS_MITIG interventions must pass ETHICS_BOUND review gate before deployment

edges.why_related: ethics bounds prohibit demographic proxy encoding in persona clusters
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fairness constraints enforced at segmentation design level
edges.risk_of_conflict: ethics constraint violation causes fairness and regulatory issues
edges.example: PERSONA_SEGMENT cluster features must pass ETHICS_BOUND protected-attribute check

edges.why_related: ethics bounds restrict which onboarding signals may be collected in cold-start
edges.benefit_of_coupling: consent and scope compliance enforced at onboarding
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-collection at cold-start violates ethics bounds
edges.example: COLD_START onboarding questions reviewed against ETHICS_BOUND collection restrictions

edges.why_related: privacy consent scopes which signal data BAYES_UPDATE may process
edges.benefit_of_coupling: posterior built only from consented data
edges.risk_of_conflict: processing beyond consent scope causes GDPR violation
edges.example: BAYES_UPDATE signal ingestion gated on PRIVACY_CONSENT scope check

edges.why_related: privacy consent limits retention window for expertise estimation signals
edges.benefit_of_coupling: expertise model built within legal retention scope
edges.risk_of_conflict: retention beyond consent limit causes regulatory violation
edges.example: EXPERT_EST feature retention capped at PRIVACY_CONSENT retention limit

edges.why_related: calibration results trigger recalibration of expertise estimator when drift detected
edges.benefit_of_coupling: expertise model stays accurate over population shifts
edges.risk_of_conflict: missed calibration allows silent expertise model degradation
edges.example: SIGNAL_CALIB drift alert on expertise signal triggers EXPERT_EST recalibration

edges.why_related: calibration monitors fatigue signal distribution and triggers recalibration on drift
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fatigue model accuracy maintained over time
edges.risk_of_conflict: undetected fatigue drift causes systematic over/under-simplification
edges.example: SIGNAL_CALIB monitors FATIGUE_EST feature distributions; alerts on PSI>0.2

edges.why_related: temporal decay modulates confidence in expertise estimates after inactivity periods
edges.benefit_of_coupling: prevents stale high-confidence expertise from harming returning users
edges.risk_of_conflict: aggressive decay erases valid long-term expertise
edges.example: TEMPORAL_DECAY applies half-life to EXPERT_EST posterior confidence on schedule

edges.why_related: overload alert triggers immediate difficulty reduction in the adaptive controller
edges.benefit_of_coupling: real-time corrective action prevents abandonment
edges.risk_of_conflict: feedback loop latency allows overload to persist before correction
edges.example: OVERLOAD_DETECT alert feeds ADAPT_DIFF emergency setpoint reduction

edges.why_related: overconfidence signal triggers specific verification-nudge intervention from BIAS_MITIG
edges.benefit_of_coupling: targeted intervention deployed when and only when overconfidence detected
edges.risk_of_conflict: overconfidence signal inaccuracy causes unnecessary interventions
edges.example: OVERCONF_DETECT active signal gates BIAS_MITIG verification-nudge deployment

edges.why_related: expertise posterior directly sets the baseline difficulty level
edges.benefit_of_coupling: difficulty anchored to user ability level
edges.risk_of_conflict: expertise miscalibration causes systematic difficulty mismatch
edges.example: EXPERT_EST posterior drives ADAPT_DIFF baseline setpoint before performance adjustment

edges.why_related: fatigue posterior triggers downward difficulty adjustment and complexity ceiling
edges.benefit_of_coupling: difficulty modulated by cognitive availability not just ability
edges.risk_of_conflict: fatigue miscalibration causes inappropriate difficulty during tired states
edges.example: FATIGUE_EST posterior lowers ADAPT_DIFF ceiling when fatigue_posterior > threshold

edges.why_related: high fatigue posterior increases overload detection sensitivity threshold
edges.benefit_of_coupling: overload detector pre-alerted to higher risk during fatigue
edges.risk_of_conflict: fatigue false-positive lowers overload threshold too aggressively
edges.example: FATIGUE_EST high posterior reduces OVERLOAD_DETECT alert threshold

edges.why_related: persona cluster prior is the main informative prior injected at cold-start
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cold-start bootstrapped with richer than population-flat prior
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong cluster assignment injects wrong prior at cold-start
edges.example: PERSONA_SEGMENT cluster assignment drives COLD_START prior selection

edges.why_related: scaffolding fade schedule determines when user is ready for metacognitive prompting
edges.benefit_of_coupling: metacognitive prompts deployed at appropriate mastery transition points
edges.risk_of_conflict: premature metacognitive prompt during scaffolding phase adds load
edges.example: METACOG_PROMPT triggered at scaffolding fade transitions in SCAFFOLDING

edges.why_related: overconfidence signal specifically triggers prediction-before-answer metacognitive prompt
edges.benefit_of_coupling: targeted prompt addresses detected overconfidence pattern
edges.risk_of_conflict: overconfidence false-positive deploys unnecessary patronizing prompt
edges.example: OVERCONF_DETECT active signal selects METACOG_PROMPT prediction-first prompt type

edges.why_related: ADAPT_DIFF adaptation events are the primary signal monitored by FEEDBACK_LOOP for loop governance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: loop governance has full visibility into adaptation decisions
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing adaptation events blind FEEDBACK_LOOP to filter-bubble formation
edges.example: FEEDBACK_LOOP monitors ADAPT_DIFF event stream for oscillation and filter-bubble signals

edges.why_related: loop audit findings from FEEDBACK_LOOP inform EVAL_UX evaluation design (exploration rate in A/B)
edges.benefit_of_coupling: evaluation captures loop health metrics as guardrails
edges.risk_of_conflict: loop audit findings ignored in evaluation leading to filter-bubble ships
edges.example: FEEDBACK_LOOP exploration rate config informs EVAL_UX A/B design parameters

edges.why_related: A/B results and offline simulation from EVAL_UX validate and recalibrate ADAPT_DIFF parameters
edges.benefit_of_coupling: difficulty controller parameters grounded in empirical evaluation
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignored A/B results allow ineffective or harmful difficulty parameters to persist
edges.example: EVAL_UX A/B results gate ADAPT_DIFF parameter updates before production deployment

edges.why_related: ecological rationality framing determines how posterior uncertainty is formatted for user communication
edges.benefit_of_coupling: uncertainty communicated in cognitively accessible format
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong framing causes user misinterpretation of uncertainty
edges.example: GIGERENZER_RISK natural-frequency format applied to BAYES_UPDATE uncertainty output

edges.why_related: numeracy estimate from EDU_EST drives format selection in GIGERENZER_RISK
edges.benefit_of_coupling: risk format matched to user numeracy level
edges.risk_of_conflict: numeracy miscalibration causes wrong risk format selection
edges.example: EDU_EST numeracy posterior selects icon-array vs natural-frequency format in GIGERENZER_RISK

edges.why_related: accumulated expertise posterior conflicts with cold-start prior reset attempts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: expertise history preserved; cold-start override resisted
edges.risk_of_conflict: cold-start override erases legitimate expertise history
edges.example: expert_est_wins_if_session_count_gt_5: cold-start must not override accumulated expertise posterior
edges.resolution_rule: cold-start must not override accumulated expertise posterior; expertise estimate wins if session count>5

edges.why_related: bias mitigation intervention design conflicts with ethics boundary constraints on coercion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ethics review gates prevent deployment of coercive mitigations
edges.risk_of_conflict: ethics constraint blocks effective but edge-case interventions
edges.example: ethics_bound_authoritative: mitigation strategy must pass ethics review before deployment
edges.resolution_rule: mitigation strategy must pass ethics review before deployment; ETHICS_BOUND is authoritative

edges.why_related: temporal decay erodes expertise posterior confidence conflicting with long-term expertise retention need
edges.benefit_of_coupling: staleness prevented; expertise naturally refreshed on return
edges.risk_of_conflict: aggressive decay punishes returning experts with valid long-term expertise
edges.example: expertise_half_life_conservative: decay half-life for expertise must be >= 14 days
edges.resolution_rule: decay half-life for expertise must be set conservatively (>=14 days) to avoid erasing legitimate long-term expertise

conflict_axes.description: Richer behavioral signal collection improves cognitive modeling accuracy but increases privacy risk and regulatory exposure
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: default to data minimization; collect only signals necessary for active personalization features

conflict_axes.description: Fast belief updates react to new evidence quickly but cause UX instability; slow updates provide stability but lag real state changes
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use asymmetric update: fast upward expertise revision, slow downward to avoid penalizing temporary errors

conflict_axes.description: More scaffolding reduces errors but can create dependency and undermine user autonomy and skill development
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: scaffold to zone of proximal development; fade monotonically with mastery signals

conflict_axes.description: Bias mitigation nudges improve decision quality but can cross into manipulative dark patterns if not carefully bounded
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: all nudges require ethics review; autonomy metric must not degrade in A/B

conflict_axes.description: Exploration rate injection prevents filter bubbles but degrades short-term UX; exploitation maximizes immediate satisfaction but creates lock-in
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: maintain minimum 5% exploration rate; review quarterly

conflict_axes.description: More onboarding questions improve cold-start accuracy but increase friction and reduce completion rates
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: limit onboarding to 3 optional questions; use population priors for remainder

conflict_axes.description: Sensitive overload and overconfidence detectors catch more true events but generate more false positives that degrade expert UX
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: tune for expert-cohort false-positive rate <0.20 as primary constraint

conflict_axes.description: Long belief half-lives preserve legitimate expertise but lock in stale fatigue or error-state beliefs
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: expertise half-life >=14 days; fatigue half-life <=2 hours

conflict_axes.description: Richer cognitive modeling produces more accurate personalization but risks crossing into clinical territory requiring regulated medical device status
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: all feature descriptions reviewed against clinical-boundary checklist; system never recommends clinical action

conflict_axes.description: Bayesian fusion of many signals produces accurate user-state estimates but reduces interpretability for UX designers debugging personalization behavior
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: produce human-readable explanation alongside posterior for each adaptation decision

edge_cases.scenario: Expert user newly onboarded to system with no history
edge_cases.risk: system initializes as novice and over-scaffolds; expert frustrated
edge_cases.mitigation: use optional role self-report in onboarding; weight role signal heavily in cold-start prior

edge_cases.scenario: High-fatigue user tackling genuinely novel complex task
edge_cases.risk: overload detector false-positives and simplifies, removing necessary information
edge_cases.mitigation: include task-novelty feature in overload model; require novelty-flag before triggering simplification

edge_cases.scenario: Non-native speaker with high domain expertise
edge_cases.risk: vocabulary-based education/expertise estimation reads low due to language effects
edge_cases.mitigation: include language-detection signal; down-weight vocabulary proxy when non-native language detected

edge_cases.scenario: User deletes all data (right-to-deletion) and immediately returns
edge_cases.risk: system reverts to cold-start but user expects continuity
edge_cases.mitigation: communicate to user that deletion resets personalization; offer lightweight re-onboarding flow

edge_cases.scenario: Long-inactive expert user returns after 90 days
edge_cases.risk: temporal decay reduces expertise belief to near-prior; returning expert gets novice UX
edge_cases.mitigation: set expertise half-life to 30 days minimum; provide explicit returning-expert re-onboarding that fast-tracks expertise re-estimation

edge_cases.scenario: User population shifts with new market launch with different literacy norms
edge_cases.risk: education and vocabulary models miscalibrated for new population leading to systematic bias
edge_cases.mitigation: trigger full signal recalibration on new market launch; maintain market-specific priors

edge_cases.scenario: Adaptive difficulty oscillates due to mis-tuned PID gains
edge_cases.risk: difficulty yo-yos between easy and hard creating confusing UX and user dropout
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce oscillation dampener: difficulty can change by at most 1 tier per 5 interactions

edge_cases.scenario: Bias mitigation nudge perceived as manipulative by user
edge_cases.risk: user distrust of system; regulatory complaint
edge_cases.mitigation: all nudges explained in plain language on demand; opt-out available; ethics review mandatory

edge_cases.scenario: Cold-start persona cluster assignment confidence below threshold
edge_cases.risk: wrong prior injected leading to systematic difficulty miscalibration
edge_cases.mitigation: cluster assignment confidence threshold; if below threshold use flat population prior instead of cluster prior

edge_cases.scenario: Overconfidence detection triggers on genuinely expert fast performance
edge_cases.risk: expert correctly bypassing obvious steps gets patronizing verification gate
edge_cases.mitigation: suppress overconfidence gate when expert_posterior > 0.80 and task tier < user expertise tier

edge_cases.scenario: Signal calibration survey data stops arriving due to survey fatigue
edge_cases.risk: calibration drift undetected; model silently degrades
edge_cases.mitigation: fallback to task-outcome ground truth when survey data sparse; alert when both signals missing >7 days

edge_cases.scenario: Regulatory change requires shorter data retention than current half-life settings
edge_cases.risk: temporal decay configuration conflicts with new legal retention limit
edge_cases.mitigation: retention policy owns hard upper bound on half-life; decay config automatically capped at retention limit

workflow.description: Define dual-process routing policy, working-memory capacity model, and cognitive load taxonomy for the product context
workflow.gate: framing doc reviewed by UX researcher and ethics officer

workflow.description: Document hard constraints: non-clinical scope, refusal rules, disclaimer requirements; complete ethics and legal review
workflow.gate: ethics review signed off; legal review complete
workflow.output: ethical constraint spec and refusal rule set

workflow.description: Define data minimization policy, consent flows, retention limits, and deletion workflows; complete DPIA
Enumerate biases relevant to UX with signal fingerprints and mitigation strategies; review against ethics spec
workflow.gate: catalog covers >=8 biases; ethics review passed

workflow.description: Build expertise, education, fatigue, and intent estimators from behavioral signals; calibrate each against labeled samples
Implement Bayesian update rule fusing all signals into joint user-state posterior; validate coverage test
Elicit population priors from historical data; build persona clusters; design optional onboarding; set cluster fairness constraints
workflow.gate: fairness audit passes; cluster stability verified

workflow.description: Set per-signal half-lives within retention policy bounds; implement staleness flags and re-estimation triggers
workflow.gate: returning-expert test passes; staleness trigger fires within 2 interactions

workflow.description: Build PID-like difficulty controller driven by user-state posterior; integrate scaffolding engine with fade schedule
workflow.gate: oscillation test passes; scaffolding fade correlates with mastery

workflow.description: Deploy overload detector and overconfidence signal; tune thresholds to meet precision and false-positive constraints
Build nudge and reframing interventions for each catalogued bias; gate on ethics review; instrument with autonomy metric
workflow.gate: ethics review per intervention; autonomy metric baseline established

workflow.description: Define A/B test design with holdout; set primary and guardrail metrics; run pilot; review results before full launch

dominance_rules.rule: ETHICS_BOUND dominates all other nodes when scope conflict detected
dominance_rules.rationale: Clinical-boundary violation is a hard regulatory and liability risk; no personalization feature overrides ethical scope
dominance_rules.condition: any feature description uses diagnostic or therapeutic framing

dominance_rules.rationale: Legal compliance (GDPR/CCPA) is non-negotiable; retention and collection must stay within consent scope
dominance_rules.condition: signal collection or retention exceeds consent scope or retention limit

dominance_rules.rule: COLD_START falls back to flat population prior when cluster confidence is low
dominance_rules.rationale: Wrong cluster prior causes systematic miscalibration; flat prior is safer than confident wrong prior

dominance_rules.rule: TEMPORAL_DECAY half-life is capped by PRIVACY_CONSENT retention limit
dominance_rules.rationale: Data retention limit is a hard legal constraint; decay configuration cannot exceed it
dominance_rules.condition: configured half-life would retain data beyond legal retention limit

dominance_rules.rule: OVERCONF_DETECT gate suppressed when expert_posterior > 0.80 and task tier < user expertise tier
dominance_rules.rationale: Verified experts on sub-expert tasks are likely correct to skip steps; gate adds noise not safety

dominance_rules.rule: ADAPT_DIFF difficulty change bounded to 1 tier per 5 interactions
dominance_rules.rationale: Rapid oscillation causes UX disorientation; stability constraint dominates optimization signal
dominance_rules.condition: proposed difficulty change would alter tier by more than 1 step in fewer than 5 interactions

dominance_rules.rule: BIAS_MITIG intervention requires confirmed bias signal before deployment
dominance_rules.rationale: Untriggered bias mitigation wastes user attention and may patronize; signal confirmation is prerequisite
dominance_rules.condition: no active bias signal fingerprint detected for the proposed intervention

dominance_rules.rule: FATIGUE_EST high-fatigue flag gates metacognitive prompts off
dominance_rules.rationale: Metacognitive prompts add cognitive load; deploying during high-fatigue states causes abandonment

dominance_rules.rule: SIGNAL_CALIB drift alert gates model update before BAYES_UPDATE processes new signals
dominance_rules.rationale: Drifted input signals corrupt the posterior; recalibration must precede continued updates
dominance_rules.condition: drift alert active on any input signal

dominance_rules.rule: EVAL_UX guardrail metric breach blocks ship decision regardless of primary metric lift
dominance_rules.rationale: Autonomy and fairness guardrails protect user trust; primary metric optimization does not override them
dominance_rules.condition: any guardrail metric below threshold in A/B results

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-specify COG_ARCH framing after ADAPT_DIFF is in production
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Changing the foundational dual-process routing policy invalidates all downstream difficulty calibration and requires full re-evaluation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change Bayesian prior specification after BAYES_UPDATE is in production without full recalibration
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Prior changes shift all posteriors; silent prior updates cause systematic miscalibration across all users

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not add new signal dimensions to BAYES_UPDATE without updating SIGNAL_CALIB calibration baseline
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Uncalibrated signals distort the posterior; each new dimension requires a calibration reference

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change temporal decay half-lives without checking PRIVACY_CONSENT retention limits
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Half-life extension may violate legal retention constraints; always check retention policy first

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy new bias mitigation interventions without ethics review
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Untested interventions risk crossing into coercion; ethics review is a hard gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not retrain PERSONA_SEGMENT clusters without re-running fairness audit
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Cluster retrain can introduce new demographic proxy correlations; fairness audit must gate each retrain

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not adjust ADAPT_DIFF oscillation bounds without re-running oscillation simulation
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Looser bounds can cause UX disorientation; simulation must confirm stability before production change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not remove EVAL_UX guardrail metrics without documented product decision
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Guardrail removal silently degrades ethical constraints; must be an explicit recorded decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change cold-start onboarding questions without re-running GDPR review
anti_rework_rules.rationale: New questions may collect additional personal data requiring updated DPIA

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not update BIAS_CATALOG without cross-checking BIAS_MITIG intervention library for stale entries
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Catalog changes may invalidate existing interventions; always propagate catalog updates to mitigation library

iteration_protocol.trigger: expertise estimate CI width > 0.40 after 10 interactions
iteration_protocol.action: increase signal feature set for EXPERT_EST; add vocabulary complexity feature

iteration_protocol.trigger: fatigue false-positive rate on novel-task cohort > 0.25
iteration_protocol.action: add task-novelty feature to FATIGUE_EST and OVERLOAD_DETECT models

iteration_protocol.trigger: Bayesian posterior coverage test fails (90% CI covers < 85% of true states)
iteration_protocol.action: revise likelihood model or prior specification in BAYES_UPDATE

iteration_protocol.trigger: A/B shows no significant lift for adaptive difficulty after 4 weeks
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine difficulty setpoint formula in ADAPT_DIFF; check if mastery signal is informative

iteration_protocol.trigger: bias mitigation A/B shows autonomy metric degraded
iteration_protocol.action: revise intervention design in BIAS_MITIG; re-run ethics review

iteration_protocol.trigger: cluster fairness audit flags proxy correlation > 0.3
iteration_protocol.action: re-cluster PERSONA_SEGMENT excluding flagged features; re-run fairness audit

iteration_protocol.trigger: signal drift detected by SIGNAL_CALIB on any signal dimension
iteration_protocol.action: pause BAYES_UPDATE updates; recalibrate drifted signal; re-enable updates

iteration_protocol.trigger: returning-expert test fails (expertise tier not preserved after 14-day absence)
iteration_protocol.action: extend expertise half-life in TEMPORAL_DECAY; re-run returning-expert test

iteration_protocol.trigger: difficulty oscillation amplitude > 15% in production monitoring
iteration_protocol.action: reduce PID gain in ADAPT_DIFF; tighten oscillation bound in FEEDBACK_LOOP

iteration_protocol.trigger: new jurisdiction regulation requires feature change
iteration_protocol.action: re-run ETHICS_BOUND and PRIVACY_CONSENT reviews; update refusal rules and retention limits
